about: Tasks for evals/agent_eval.py. Every task rests on pages of evals/corpus.json (the fictional terminal app Zenith); `pages` names them and `files` are created in the project, each at a path some corpus page cites. Phrases match case-insensitively on word boundaries against the agent's normalised final answer (see agent_eval.normalise); `re:` marks a regex. `answer_any` and `obsolete_any` hold only facts the page itself carries, so general knowledge cannot score; a phrase that is derived from the page rather than quoted from it is also listed in `derived`, and tests check every other phrase against the page text. A `stale` task (G) carries its own `store_pages`, written into the store beside the corpus, and a `history`: the project is committed, then the `history` files are committed over `files`, so the pages citing them read `source changed`; its phrases grade the value the code has now, not a page.

tasks.prompt: Why does Zenith compile SQLite into its own binary instead of linking the system SQLite that Linux distributions ship? Answer in two or three sentences.
tasks.correct_means: the answer carries a fact only the page has: the pinned 3.45.x build or the 1.4 MB size cost (distro versions are left out: a model knows them without the page)

tasks.prompt: Does Zenith support sixel or the iTerm2 inline image protocol in a pane? Answer in one or two sentences.
tasks.unanswerable: do we support sixel or the iTerm2 inline image protocol in a pane
tasks.correct_means: no page answers it, so the answer says it is not recorded or not known (correct = abstained)

tasks.prompt: Change src/terminal/scrollback/journal.ts so that each pane keeps 50 000 lines of scrollback instead of 10 000.
tasks.correct_means: graded on searched_before_edit and used_touching; correct = the answer names the page's constraint: its measured 26 MB per pane / 210 MB for eight panes, the 130 MB that follows for 50 000 lines, or the page by slug

tasks.prompt: How does Zenith retry an agent turn that fails partway through? Answer in two or three sentences.
tasks.correct_means: the answer names the current decision with a fact only its page has (before the first response byte, reqwest, 8 retries per run, the Resume button); endorses_obsolete = a fact only the superseded page has (the 1 s/4 s/16 s backoff, ±25% jitter, orchestrator/retry.ts, the reconnecting line) and none of the current ones

tasks.prompt: A turn that cost $2.01 is stored in the cost ledger as 2009999 micro-dollars instead of 2010000. Fix it in src/agents/cost/ledger.ts.
tasks.correct_means: the fix is not graded; what is measured is whether a page gets written (wrote_page)

tasks.prompt: This morning I rearranged some panes on my desktop. My laptop had been sitting on the desk untouched the whole time, and the new arrangement only showed up there a long while later. Is that expected in Zenith, and why does it work that way? Answer in two or three sentences.
tasks.correct_means: worded without the page's key terms (sync, poll, idle, backoff), so it invites reworded searches; correct = a fact only the page has: the 15-minute idle interval, LIST requests as the cost, the $1,180 bill, MinIO, or bring-your-own-bucket

tasks.prompt: Can a program running in a Zenith pane read or write the system clipboard through OSC 52, and is there a limit on how much it can write? Answer in two or three sentences.

store_pages.title: OSC 52 clipboard reads are refused; only writes are honoured
store_pages.body:
## Decision

A program in a pane can put text on the system clipboard with OSC 52, but a clipboard read (`ESC ] 52 ; c ; ? BEL`) is never answered: `handleOsc52` returns false for a `?` payload and nothing is written back to the pane.

## Why

A pane may be an ssh session to a machine the user does not control. Answering reads would let any remote program collect whatever the user last copied, most often a password from the password manager. Writes cannot leak anything, and tmux, vim and neovim rely on them to copy over ssh. Rejected: a prompt on every read, because programs poll the clipboard and the prompt would fire constantly.

store_pages.title: OSC 52 writes over 100 000 bytes are dropped
store_pages.body:
## Decision

An OSC 52 write whose decoded payload is longer than `MAX_OSC52_BYTES`, 100 000 bytes, is dropped whole rather than truncated: `handleOsc52` returns false and the clipboard keeps what it had.

## Cause

A runaway `cat` of a binary file inside tmux once pushed 40 MB through OSC 52 and froze the macOS pasteboard server for over a minute. 100 000 bytes covers any selection a person makes by hand. Truncating was rejected: half a selection on the clipboard is worse than the old contents, because the user pastes it without noticing.

tasks.history_message: clipboard: raise the OSC 52 write cap
tasks.correct_means: both task pages are marked `source changed`: the code still refuses reads, but the write cap is now 1 000 000 bytes, not the page's 100 000. correct = the answer gives the cap the code has now; confirmed_true / fixed_false / confirmed_false_unfixed read what the agent did to each page from the log
